question.text: In the hydrogen atom spectrum, <math><msub><mrow><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> represent wavelengths emitted due to transition from second and first excited states to the ground state respectively. The ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mfrac></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>q</mi></math> are the smallest positive integers. What is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>?
